- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 10–15 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then drop sharply, suggesting overshoot after initial spikes.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias — forecasts often revert to lower levels after initial high peaks, but not always in sync with true price behavior.
- Late-period forecasts (last 5–10 days) are often too low, indicating underestimation of downward trends or delayed reaction to market signals.
- Model exhibits lagged response to recent price drops — true prices often dip before model catches up.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the first 5–7 days of the 30d window, then gradually adjust downward — suggesting a built-in “overconfidence” bias.
- Model fails to capture sharp, short-term reversals — especially when true prices drop rapidly after a spike.
- Forecasts show persistent upward bias in the first 10 days, then downward bias in the last 10 days — suggesting a “U-shaped” forecast error pattern.
- Model underestimates the magnitude of price corrections after spikes — true prices often fall more sharply than forecasted.
- Model tends to overfit recent trends, leading to overreaction to short-term volatility, especially in the first 5–10 days.
